title: SOA-to-Agentic AI Terminology Mapping
description: A structured mapping between Service-Oriented Architecture (SOA) concepts and their Agentic AI equivalents, offered as a starting vocabulary for the agentic enterprise. Not a claim on SOA as original work — an accelerant borrowed from a precedent the industry already validated.

mappings.soa_description: A discrete unit of functionality that can be accessed remotely and acted upon independently, deployed and versioned on its own so that changing it does not require changing its consumers.
mappings.agentic_description: An autonomous AI entity that can perform specific tasks, make decisions, and interact with other agents, choosing how to accomplish an objective rather than following a fixed sequence of steps.

mappings.soa_description: Architectural approach using small, independently deployable services, each owning a narrow slice of business capability so teams can build, release, and scale them separately.
mappings.agentic_description: Specialized, focused AI agents designed for specific tasks within larger systems, narrow enough to be reasoned about, tested, and replaced individually rather than as part of one monolithic agent.

mappings.soa_description: Reusable services that provide shared functionality across multiple applications — authentication, notification, document generation — maintained once and consumed everywhere.
mappings.agentic_description: Reusable AI capabilities and functions that agents can utilize to perform common tasks, exposed as a shared library so every agent does not reimplement the same retrieval, extraction, or calculation.

mappings.soa_description: A formal specification defining how to interact with a service, including inputs, outputs, and constraints, so consumers integrate against the contract rather than the implementation.
mappings.agentic_description: A specification defining an agent's capabilities, interaction protocols, and behavioral constraints — what it may do on its own, what it must escalate, and what callers can rely on.

mappings.soa_description: A directory where services are published and can be discovered by consumers, holding the endpoint, version, and contract for each registered service.
mappings.agentic_description: A repository where agents are registered and can be discovered by other agents or orchestrators, recording each agent's capabilities, ownership, and permitted scope.

mappings.soa_description: A dynamic mechanism for locating available services at runtime, resolving which instance to call as deployments scale up and down.
mappings.agentic_description: A dynamic mechanism for locating available agents and their current capabilities at runtime, so work is routed to whichever agent is actually able and permitted to handle it.

mappings.soa_description: Enterprise service bus providing message routing, transformation, and integration capabilities, so systems that do not share a data format can still exchange work.
mappings.agentic_description: Central orchestration layer managing agent lifecycle, routing, and coordination, carrying work between agents and the systems they act on.

mappings.soa_description: A single entry point managing routing, security, authentication, and rate limiting for service consumers, so those concerns are handled once at the edge rather than in every service.
mappings.agentic_description: A single entry point managing routing, authentication, and rate limiting for external systems and human users interacting with agents, and the place where access policy is applied.

mappings.soa_description: Coordinating multiple services to execute complex business processes, with the sequence, branching, and error handling defined centrally.
mappings.agentic_description: System that coordinates multiple agents to execute complex automated workflows, assigning work, tracking progress, and deciding what happens when an agent fails or escalates.

mappings.soa_description: A peer-to-peer collaboration pattern where services interact directly via events, without central control over the sequence.
mappings.agentic_description: A peer-to-peer collaboration pattern where agents coordinate directly through shared events or signals, without a central orchestrator directing each step.

mappings.soa_description: Combining multiple services to create higher-level business functionality, so a complete process can be assembled from parts built independently.
mappings.agentic_description: Combining multiple agents to create complex autonomous systems and workflows, assembling specialists into something that completes an end-to-end process.

mappings.soa_description: Services are designed to have minimal dependencies on each other, so one can change or fail without forcing changes elsewhere.
mappings.agentic_description: Agents operate independently with minimal dependencies, making autonomous decisions within their granted scope rather than waiting on a controller for every step.

mappings.soa_description: The level of functionality encapsulated within a single service, and the trade-off between many small services and fewer larger ones.
mappings.agentic_description: The breadth and depth of responsibilities assigned to a specific agent, which determines both what it can accomplish alone and how much of the system its failures reach.

mappings.soa_description: A design preference that services not retain client state between calls, so any instance can serve any request.
mappings.agentic_description: An explicit definition of what an agent retains in operational memory between interactions and what it deliberately discards — since useful agents often need memory rather than none.

mappings.soa_description: A property ensuring repeated calls produce the same effect as a single call, making retries safe after a timeout or partial failure.
mappings.agentic_description: A property ensuring a repeated agent action produces the same effect as a single execution, which matters more here because retries are often decided autonomously.

mappings.soa_description: A resilience pattern that halts calls to a failing service to prevent cascading failure, resuming only once it recovers.
mappings.agentic_description: A resilience pattern that halts delegation to a failing or underperforming agent and reroutes to a fallback agent or human escalation, rather than simply stopping.

mappings.soa_description: Architecture where services respond to and produce events for loose coupling, with producers unaware of which consumers will react.
mappings.agentic_description: Event-based activation mechanisms that prompt agents to take specific actions, so work begins when a condition is met rather than when someone invokes it.

mappings.soa_description: Structured communication patterns between services, defining request/response, publish/subscribe, and the message shapes each side expects.
mappings.agentic_description: Standardized methods for agents to exchange information and coordinate actions, covering not just message format but how intent, context, and results are conveyed.

mappings.soa_description: Standard protocols for web service communication and data exchange, such as SOAP and REST over HTTP.
mappings.agentic_description: Standardized interfaces and protocols for agent communication and integration, so agents built on different platforms work together without bespoke adapters.

mappings.soa_description: Ability of different systems and services to work together effectively, across vendors, platforms, and data formats.
mappings.agentic_description: Protocols and standards enabling agents from different systems to collaborate, so a multi-agent workflow is not confined to one vendor's runtime.

mappings.soa_description: Standard patterns for integrating enterprise applications and services — named solutions to recurring routing, transformation, and messaging problems.
mappings.agentic_description: Reusable design patterns for agent interaction, coordination, and integration, giving teams a shared name for structures they would otherwise reinvent.

mappings.soa_description: A shared, standardized data schema used across services to avoid point-to-point translation between every pair of systems.
mappings.agentic_description: A shared, standardized schema for context entities so agents interpret the same situational data consistently across an enterprise, rather than each holding its own view.

mappings.soa_description: The two parties in a service interaction: the caller and the service being called.
mappings.agentic_description: The two parties in an agent-fulfilled intent: whoever originates the request — a person, another agent, or an orchestrator — and whichever agent fulfills it.

mappings.soa_description: Managing multiple concurrent versions of a service interface as it evolves, so existing consumers keep working while new ones adopt the change.
mappings.agentic_description: Managing multiple concurrent versions of an agent's skill set or behavior as it evolves through feedback and memory updates, so changes are traceable rather than silent.

mappings.soa_description: Creating virtual representations of services for testing and development, so teams can build against dependencies that are unavailable or costly to call.
mappings.agentic_description: Creating test agents by abstracting real-world conditions for testing, training, and development purposes, so behavior can be exercised safely before it touches production work.

mappings.soa_description: Service Level Agreement defining performance, availability, and quality metrics, and what happens when they are not met.
mappings.agentic_description: Quality of Service metrics defining agent performance, reliability, and response standards, including accuracy and escalation rates alongside latency and uptime.

mappings.soa_description: An internal target metric that supports meeting an external SLA, set tighter than the commitment to leave room to recover.
mappings.agentic_description: An internal target metric supporting an agent's external QoS commitments, tracked continuously so degradation is caught before it breaches the commitment.

mappings.soa_description: Policies, processes, and controls for managing services throughout their lifecycle, from approval and deployment to retirement.
mappings.agentic_description: Framework for managing agent behavior, compliance, ethics, and lifecycle management, including audit trails, human oversight, and accountability for autonomous decisions.
